subject: sentences
title: What Is It Mostly About?
about: Short true texts about animals, weather and community helpers, each followed by a question: what is it mostly about, which detail tells a fact, what would be a good title, or what a word in the text means. NC RI.1.2 asks first graders to name the main topic of an information text and retell its key details, and RI.1.4 to ask and answer questions about what a word means.
tip: After he answers, ask him to say the big idea in his own words, then one small detail he remembers.

cards.q: An elephant has a long trunk. It drinks with its trunk. It sprays water too. What is this mostly about?
cards.note: Every sentence tells about the elephant and its trunk, so the main topic is an elephant.

cards.q: Wind is moving air. It can push a kite up high. Strong wind can bend trees. What is this mostly about?
cards.note: Each sentence tells something about wind. Wind is the main topic.

cards.q: A mail carrier brings letters. He walks from house to house. He has a big bag. What is this mostly about?
cards.note: The main topic is the person every sentence is about: a mail carrier.

cards.q: Penguins are birds. They cannot fly. But they can swim very fast. What is this mostly about?
cards.note: Penguins is the main topic. Every sentence is about penguins.

cards.q: A crossing guard stops the cars. She holds up a sign. Then the kids cross. What is this all about?
cards.note: The cars, the sign and the kids are details. The whole text is about a crossing guard.

cards.q: A ladybug is a small red bug. It has black spots. It eats tiny pests. What is this all about?
cards.note: The spots and the pests are details. The main topic is a ladybug.

cards.q: Ants are strong. One ant can lift a big crumb. Ants live in groups. Which detail shows ants are strong?
cards.note: A detail is a small fact. Lifting a big crumb shows how strong an ant is.

cards.q: Clouds are tiny drops of water. When the drops get heavy, rain falls. What are clouds made of?
cards.note: The first sentence gives the detail: clouds are tiny drops of water.

cards.q: A vet is a doctor for animals. She checks a sick dog. She helps a cat get well. Who does a vet help?
cards.note: The first sentence tells you: a vet is a doctor for animals.

cards.q: The sun is a star. It gives us light and heat. Plants need it to grow. What does the sun give us?
cards.note: The second sentence has the detail: light and heat.

cards.q: A bunny has long ears. They help it hear well. It hops on strong back legs. Which detail tells how it moves?
cards.note: The ears are about hearing. The last sentence tells how a bunny moves: it hops.

cards.q: A farmer grows food. He plants corn in spring. He picks it in the fall. When does he pick the corn?
cards.note: Spring is when he plants. Look for the sentence about picking: in the fall.

cards.q: Whales live in the sea. They are very big. They come up to breathe air. What is a good title?
cards.note: A good title tells the main topic. This text is all about whales.

cards.q: A dentist takes care of teeth. He counts your teeth. He shows you how to brush. What is a good title?
cards.note: Every sentence is about the dentist, so The Dentist is a good title.

cards.q: Rain falls from clouds. It fills the rivers. Plants drink it up. What is a good title?
cards.note: The title should name the main topic. Rain is in every sentence.

cards.q: A squirrel has a bushy tail. It hides nuts in the fall. It eats them in winter. What is a good title?
cards.note: A good title fits the main topic: a busy squirrel hiding and eating nuts.

cards.q: Ducks have webbed feet. Thin skin joins the toes. The webs push the water. What does webbed mean?
cards.note: The second sentence tells what webbed means: thin skin joins the toes.

cards.q: A firefighter puts out fires. She wears a helmet. A helmet is a hard hat. What is a helmet?
cards.note: The text tells you: a helmet is a hard hat. It keeps her head safe.
